status_summary: Neither the PCAOB nor FINRA has been abolished or merged into the SEC. On the PCAOB, the House-passed reconciliation bill (H.R. 1, passed 2025-05-22) would have moved the board's duties to the SEC and ended the fees that fund it, but the Senate parliamentarian ruled on 2025-06-19 that the provision violated the Byrd rule, and the enacted law (Public Law 119-21, 2025-07-04) shows no PCAOB section in its table of contents (its Banking Committee title has four sections, none on the PCAOB); no standalone bill was found. The SEC instead changed PCAOB leadership (acting chair 2025-07-21; a new chairman and three new members appointed 2026-01-30). On FINRA, H.R. 2689 (Rep. McClain, introduced 2025-04-07) would transfer the authorities of national securities associations to the SEC two years after enactment; the House Capital Markets Subcommittee held a hearing on self-regulatory organizations on 2026-03-05, and no markup was found. The Supreme Court denied review in Alpine Securities v. FINRA on 2025-06-02, leaving FINRA's structure in place. On 2026-03-27 the Sixth Circuit denied an individual's petition for review of an SEC order upholding FINRA sanctions (No. 24-3907), holding that FINRA had jurisdiction over a person controlling a member and declining to reach an unexhausted jury-trial claim, and it denied rehearing en banc on 2026-07-16; no court has held FINRA's structure invalid. The chapter's fallback FINRA reforms and the 18-month report on other self-regulatory organizations were not found. Through 2026 both bodies continued to operate under SEC oversight: the SEC approved the PCAOB's fiscal year 2026 budget and support fee by an order dated 2026-01-22, and FINRA's board reports of 2026-06-11 and 2026-10-08 describe rule proposals under its FINRA Forward modernization effort to be filed with the SEC. GovInfo bill status shows H.R. 2689 with no action after its 2025-04-07 referral.

timeline.event: Rep. McClain introduces H.R. 2689, which would transfer the authorities and duties of registered national securities associations (in practice FINRA) to the SEC two years after enactment; referred to the House Financial Services Committee.

House passes H.R. 1, 215-214 with one present (Roll no. 145), per GovInfo bill status; trade press describes the House-passed text as transferring the PCAOB's duties to the SEC within one year and ending the accounting support fees that fund the board. The engrossed bill's table of contents lists a Public Company Accounting Oversight Board provision as Sec. 50002 in Title V (Committee on Financial Services); the operative text was beyond the readable portion of the page.
Supreme Court denies certiorari in Alpine Securities Corp. v. FINRA, leaving FINRA's structure in place; Alpine's constitutional claims continue in the district court.

Senate parliamentarian rules that the PCAOB provision in the Senate Banking Committee's reconciliation text falls under the Byrd rule, so it would need 60 votes; the SEC chair had said the SEC could fund the PCAOB's functions if the provision passed.

Public Law 119-21 enacted; the Banking Committee title (Title III) lists four sections (CFPB funding cap, a green retrofit rescission, an SEC Reserve Fund and Defense Production Act appropriations), none on the PCAOB.
SEC announces George Botic will serve as acting chair of the PCAOB.

SEC appoints Demetrios (Jim) Logothetis as PCAOB chairman and Mark Calabria, Kyle Hauptman and Steven Laughton as board members; Botic remains a member. The PCAOB lists three as sworn in from 2026-02-10 and Hauptman on 2026-08-10.

House Financial Services Subcommittee on Capital Markets holds a hearing on self-regulatory organizations including FINRA and the MSRB, considering Rep. McClain's bill to move FINRA's rulemaking, examination and enforcement authority to the SEC; no markup or vote is reported.

The Sixth Circuit (No. 24-3907) denied an individual's petition for review of an SEC order upholding FINRA sanctions, holding that FINRA had disciplinary jurisdiction over a person controlling a member firm and declining to reach a jury-trial claim not first raised before the SEC; it did not rule on FINRA's structure.
